items.item: The Variable-size Binary View Layout's 16-byte view: inline for <=12 bytes, else length/prefix/buffer-index/offset

items.item: Dictionary-encoded arrays store integer indices into a separate dictionary array; the dictionary may contain duplicates or nulls

items.item: Run-end encoding stores run_ends and values child arrays; run_ends holds cumulative end index, enabling binary-search random access unlike classic RLE

at.step: Reveal: run-end encoding

items.item: The List layout is two buffers (validity bitmap, offsets) plus a child array — the same primitive buffer kinds as flat types

items.item: A record batch is an ordered collection of same-length arrays forming a schema; the IPC protocol reconstructs them without memory copying

items.item: The validity-bitmap-absence claim is checked directly on this sandbox's installed PyArrow 26.0.0 (buffers()[0] is None for a 0-null array), not merely quoted from the spec's own permissive 'may choose' language

items.item: Dictionary encoding and run-end encoding are shown as specialists for different data shapes, not as a strictly-better/strictly-worse pair — the reveal measures a real counter-case (alternating values) where run-end encoding is worse than the plain array and dictionary encoding wins

at.step: Reveal: run-end encoding

items.item: The string-view layout's byte-level claims are measured directly from this sandbox's own PyArrow string_view() cast; only the cross-engine ClickBench performance number is disclosed as sourced-only, since DataFusion itself is not installed here

items.item: The compute-kernel speed claim is measured as a real timed ratio on this sandbox (pc.sum over 2,000,000 ints vs. an equivalent Python loop), with the assertion in examples.py using a conservative lower bound rather than the exact measured ratio, so it won't flake on a slower machine

at.step: Reveal: compute kernels
